title: tests.py runs a new small suite under a ceiling file, and the old suite, the stress suite, their callers, CI jobs and test rules are cut to match
goal: Every old _tools/test_*.py, test_stress.py, stress_test.py and testmap.py is deleted and every caller changed; a new suite written from scratch holds 60 to 100 test ids in 10 to 15 files: leak and redaction scans, the operator-only gate classes, the check-program allowlist, kbingest's untrusted-repo guards, check.py over the live kb, the lookup eval, one end-to-end scenario each for sync, pre-push, land and publish, and the ceiling's planted failure; python3 _tools/tests.py takes at most 20 s on the macOS host and 60 s on the Windows host; _tools/tests_ceiling.json (max ids, files, seconds) is enforced by tests.py on every run, and its numbers are accepted only when an active operator decision of kb/_self records them; the perfcheck id baseline and test_ids_dropped.txt are reset to the new suite; .gitlab-ci.yml and .github/workflows/kb.yml run the minimum that still gives kbgit.py publish a CI verdict; kb/_self (code.md, backlog.md, maintaining.md, tools.md), the skills and kb-worker.md allow a test only for one command's main path, one planted failure per gate, a machine-read format or a leak or untrusted-code guard, ask a retrospective instead of a regression test for a bug a log can show, and cite no tests.py -k selector that selects nothing

gates.question: Which numbers does the ceiling file _tools/tests_ceiling.json hold?
options: ids and files equal to the landed suite's counts, seconds 20, 60 and 60
gates.recommendation: ids and files equal to the landed suite's counts, seconds 20, 60 and 60

gates.question: Which test jobs stay in .gitlab-ci.yml and .github/workflows/kb.yml?
options: GitLab: kb-tests on Linux and kb-tests-windows, both manual; GitHub: one job
GitLab: kb-tests-windows only; GitHub: one job
one Linux job on each forge
gates.recommendation: GitLab: kb-tests-windows only; GitHub: one job
gates.answer: GitLab: kb-tests on Linux and kb-tests-windows, both manual; GitHub: one job (the development host is macOS, so Linux and Windows both run on GitLab)

gates.question: Does the gate keep testmap.py's map from changed paths to test files?
options: delete testmap.py: tests.py --changed runs nothing for the backlog and query log store, the suite without git scenarios for kb content, the whole suite for anything else
keep testmap.py, trimmed to the new files
gates.recommendation: delete testmap.py: tests.py --changed runs nothing for the backlog and query log store, the suite without git scenarios for kb content, the whole suite for anything else
gates.answer: delete testmap.py: tests.py --changed runs nothing for the backlog and query log store, the suite without git scenarios for kb content, the whole suite for anything else

notes: Merged from EP-5o2drech, its ten stories and ST-h6qyvynp, ST-w5mrjyyw, ST-5rjig6fj, ST-4me7hv37, ST-jcbbt6wl (dropped 2026-10-05; git keeps them). Operator's direction of 2026-10-05: cut aggressively; errors are read from ops rows and querylog.py digest; a later break is a bug and a retrospective. Earlier operator answers carried over: new-test rule 'minimal' (one command's main path, one planted failure per gate, a machine-read format, a leak or untrusted-code guard; at most two parametrize cases; no test of doc wording; no regression test for a defect a log shows); stress suite 'delete'; CI 'windows-only'; EP-hlnsqx4f's retitle (drop 'with no lost coverage') is still the operator's. Before: 4,168 ids, 103 files, 305-377 s on macOS, about 25 min on the Windows host; stress 55 s and 462 s; GitLab kb-tests 812 s, kb-tests-windows 2,200 s. Old tests whose subject stays (to read, not copy): gate_authority_refuses_an_agent_an_operator_class, authority_refused_class, authority_trust_boundary, backlog_check_refuses_leak_in_item_text, check_program_allowlist_refuses, kbingest map guards (ast shadow, symlink, scrub_env, program inside the worktree, redact_leaks), sync failing_gate_blocks_a_plain_push and content_only_goes_to_main, publish leaked_address and query_log_store_is_refused, backlog_land_content_item_in_one_run, lookup_eval_passes, check_py_passes, test_kb_leaks.py, test_redact.py. Stress callers: tests.py, testmap.py, conftest.py, perfcheck.py, bl_base.REVIEW_CHECKS, bl_intake.HEAVY_SCRIPTS, bl_land, bl_selfcheck, backlog.py, settings.json, session_start.py, cleanhost-run.ps1, both CI files, pyproject.toml, four skills, kb-worker.md, kb/_self docs. kb/_self cited 229 tests.py -k selectors (181 distinct). Publish's CI verdict (kbpublic.ci_refusals) needs a pipeline of the source commit with no failed job script. The checks pass before the work except tests.py --ceiling, which does not exist yet.
